site.title: Magpie · Save it in a tap, let your own AI file it into your notes
site.description: Magpie is a self-hostable inbox. Save links and images from any device, and an AI agent on your own computer reads them and files them into your Obsidian vault.
site.nav.label: Page navigation
site.hero.title: Save it in a tap. Your own AI files it into your notes.
site.hero.lead: See a link or an image worth keeping? Send it to Magpie. An agent on your own computer reads it, writes the summary and files it into your Obsidian vault, so nothing rots in a read-later pile.
site.hero.note: Every account gets its own private space, and the processing happens on your own computer.

site.how.title: From “saw it” to “filed it” in three steps
site.how.lead: Collecting happens in the cloud. The reading and writing happen on your own computer.
site.how.step1.title: Save from anywhere
site.how.step1.body: Tap a shortcut in the iPhone share sheet, or send links and images from anything that can make a web request.
site.how.step2.title: It lands in your private inbox
site.how.step2.body: Every item belongs to your account alone. The web inbox shows where each one stands at any moment.
site.how.step3.title: Your local agent files it
site.how.step3.body: A daemon on your computer picks up the task, has Codex or Claude Code read the page, writes the note into your Obsidian vault, and reports a summary back to the inbox.
site.features.title: Details built for the long run
site.features.lead: Capture has to be quick, processing has to be dependable, and the data has to stay in your hands.
site.feature.capture.title: One-tap capture
site.feature.capture.body: Save a link, a paragraph with links in it, or an image. Several links in one message become separate items automatically.
site.feature.agent.title: Your own agent and model
site.feature.agent.body: The daemon drives Codex or Claude Code on your computer through the ACP protocol, using the login or subscription you already have.
site.feature.local.title: Notes are written on your computer only
site.feature.local.body: Processing is local and the result goes straight into your vault folder. The cloud keeps only the link, its status and a short summary.
site.feature.status.title: Visible progress, self-recovering queue
site.feature.status.body: Every item has a clear status. Tasks whose daemon went quiet return to the queue on their own, repeated failures say why, and you can always run one again.
site.feature.keys.title: Least-privilege access keys
site.feature.keys.body: A shortcut's key can only save. A daemon's key can only process tasks. Each key can expire and can be revoked on its own.
site.feature.data.title: Take your data with you
site.feature.data.body: Export everything in one click, delete single items or the whole account, and review 180 days of sign-in and key activity.
site.feature.multi.title: Multi-user, fully isolated
site.feature.multi.body: Share one instance with family or a team. Nobody sees anyone else's items, images or keys, and the app has no see-everything admin view.
site.feature.cloud.title: No server to look after
site.feature.cloud.body: The service runs on Cloudflare: one Worker, one database and one private storage bucket.
site.trust.title: Built to trust nothing by default
site.trust.lead: Every request has to prove who it is and what it is allowed to do.
site.trust.point1: All reads and writes are scoped to the identity the server verified. A user ID sent along with a request changes nothing.
site.trust.point2: Images sit in private storage and ownership is checked on every read. Knowing the link is not enough.
site.trust.point3: A key is shown once, when it is created. The server stores only a hash it cannot reverse.
site.trust.point4: Managing keys, changing sign-in methods and deleting the account all require a browser sign-in. No key can do them.
site.trust.point5: A fresh instance starts with sign-up closed. The administrator's email creates the first account.

site.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
site.faq.a1: No. The daemon on your computer does the processing and writes notes straight into your local vault. The server stores only the links and images you send, their status, and the summary and result location the daemon reports back.
site.faq.q2: Do I need my own AI model?
site.faq.a2: You need Codex or Claude Code on your computer. The daemon uses its existing login or subscription, or an endpoint and key you configure instead.
site.faq.a3: Not yet. Images are stored and viewable, but they don't go through processing for now.
site.faq.q4: What happens to things I save while my computer is off?
site.faq.a4: Nothing is lost. Items wait in your inbox, and the daemon picks them up the next time it runs.
site.faq.q5: Can several people share one instance?
site.faq.a5: Yes. Once the administrator opens sign-up, everyone signs in with their own account, data stays separate, and each person connects their own computer and vault.
site.faq.q6: What if I want to leave?
site.faq.a6: Export everything from account settings, then delete your account. Its links, images, keys and activity log are removed with it.
site.cta.title: Give the good things you find somewhere to go
site.cta.body: Sign in, create an access key, and save your first item within minutes.
site.footer.tagline: Save it in a tap. Your own AI files it into your notes.
